For statistical analysis, you can use Lee's L statistic for bivariate spatial correlation analysis, or another appropriate method of your choosing. You are testing whether Gas in one place relates to GHG in NEIGHBORING places.

Determine whether the two variables show a significant bivariate spatial relationship. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement this directly using only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = "chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_gas_ghg.csv"
ADJACENCY_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# sort df
df = df.sort_values('borough').reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Check symmetry of adjacency
adj_set = set()
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b = row['borough']
    neigh = row['neighbor']
    adj_set.add((b, neigh))

missing = []
for b, neigh in adj_set:
    if (neigh, b) not in adj_set:
        missing.append((b, neigh))

print("Number of directed edges:", len(adj_set))
print("Number of missing reverse edges:", len(missing))
if missing:
    print("Examples:", missing[:10])

# Build binary adjacency matrix
W_binary = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    W_binary[i, j] = 1

# Check if symmetric
print("W_binary symmetric?", np.allclose(W_binary, W_binary.T))

# Row-standardize
row_sums = W_binary.sum(axis=1)
print("Row sums min, max, mean:", row_sums.min(), row_sums.max(), row_sums.mean())
print("Any zero row sums?", np.any(row_sums == 0))

W = W_binary / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]
print("W row sums (should be 1):", W.sum(axis=1)[:5])

# Get values
gas = df['Gas_value'].values
ghg = df['GHG_value'].values

# Center
gas_c = gas - gas.mean()
ghg_c = ghg - ghg.mean()

# Compute Lee's L
numerator = gas_c @ (W @ ghg_c)
denominator = np.sqrt((gas_c @ gas_c) * (ghg_c @ ghg_c))
L_obs = numerator / denominator

print("Numerator:", numerator)
print("Denominator:", denominator)
print("Lee's L:", L_obs)

# Permutation test
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 1000
L_perms = np.empty(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    ghg_perm = np.random.permutation(ghg_c)
    num_perm = gas_c @ (W @ ghg_perm)
    den_perm = np.sqrt((gas_c @ gas_c) * (ghg_perm @ ghg_perm))
    L_perms[i] = num_perm / den_perm

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = (np.sum(np.abs(L_perms) >= np.abs(L_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
print("p-value (two-tailed):", p_value)

# Also compute one-tailed for positive
p_pos = (np.sum(L_perms >= L_obs) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
p_neg = (np.sum(L_perms <= L_obs) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
print("p-value (one-tailed positive):", p_pos)
print("p-value (one-tailed negative):", p_neg)
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = "chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_gas_ghg.csv"
ADJACENCY_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)
df = df.sort_values('borough').reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build binary adjacency matrix
W_binary = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    W_binary[i, j] = 1

# Check for self-loops
self_loops = np.diag(W_binary).sum()
print("Self-loops:", self_loops)

# Row-standardized W
row_sums = W_binary.sum(axis=1)
W = W_binary / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

gas = df['Gas_value'].values
ghg = df['GHG_value'].values
gas_c = gas - gas.mean()
ghg_c = ghg - ghg.mean()

# Lee's L with row-standardized W
num_rs = gas_c @ (W @ ghg_c)
den = np.sqrt((gas_c @ gas_c) * (ghg_c @ ghg_c))
L_rs = num_rs / den
print("Lee's L (row-standardized W):", L_rs)

# Lee's L with binary W (using S0 factor)
S0 = W_binary.sum()
num_bin = gas_c @ (W_binary @ ghg_c)
L_bin = (n / S0) * num_bin / den
print("Lee's L (binary W):", L_bin)
print("S0:", S0)

# Simple Pearson correlation
pearson = np.corrcoef(gas, ghg)[0, 1]
print("Pearson r (Gas, GHG):", pearson)

# Correlation between Gas and spatial lag of GHG (row-standardized)
lag_ghg = W @ ghg
corr_gas_lagghg = np.corrcoef(gas, lag_ghg)[0, 1]
print("Corr(Gas, lag GHG):", corr_gas_lagghg)

# Moran's I for Gas
I_gas = (n / S0) * (gas_c @ (W_binary @ gas_c)) / (gas_c @ gas_c)
print("Moran's I for Gas:", I_gas)

# Moran's I for GHG
I_ghg = (n / S0) * (ghg_c @ (W_binary @ ghg_c)) / (ghg_c @ ghg_c)
print("Moran's I for GHG:", I_ghg)

# Permutation test with row-standardized W, 1000 shuffles
np.random.seed(123)
n_perm = 1000
L_perms = np.empty(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    perm_idx = np.random.permutation(n)
    ghg_perm = ghg_c[perm_idx]
    num_perm = gas_c @ (W @ ghg_perm)
    den_perm = np.sqrt((gas_c @ gas_c) * (ghg_perm @ ghg_perm))
    L_perms[i] = num_perm / den_perm

p_two = (np.sum(np.abs(L_perms) >= np.abs(L_rs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
print("Two-tailed p (1000 perm):", p_two)

# Also try 5000 permutations for stability
np.random.seed(456)
n_perm2 = 5000
L_perms2 = np.empty(n_perm2)
for i in range(n_perm2):
    perm_idx = np.random.permutation(n)
    ghg_perm = ghg_c[perm_idx]
    num_perm = gas_c @ (W @ ghg_perm)
    den_perm = np.sqrt((gas_c @ gas_c) * (ghg_perm @ ghg_perm))
    L_perms2[i] = num_perm / den_perm

p_two2 = (np.sum(np.abs(L_perms2) >= np.abs(L_rs)) + 1) / (n_perm2 + 1)
print("Two-tailed p (5000 perm):", p_two2)
print("Mean of |L_perms|:", np.mean(np.abs(L_perms)))
print("Std of L_perms:", np.std(L_perms))
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = "chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_gas_ghg.csv"
ADJACENCY_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)
df = df.sort_values('borough').reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build binary adjacency matrix (symmetric, no self-loops)
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    W[borough_to_idx[row['borough']], borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]] = 1

S0 = W.sum()
print("n:", n, "S0:", S0)

gas = df['Gas_value'].values
ghg = df['GHG_value'].values
gas_c = gas - gas.mean()
ghg_c = ghg - ghg.mean()

# Lee's L statistic (Lee 2001, 2004)
# L = (n / S0) * (z_x' W z_y) / sqrt((z_x' z_x)(z_y' z_y))
numerator = gas_c @ (W @ ghg_c)
denominator = np.sqrt((gas_c @ gas_c) * (ghg_c @ ghg_c))
L_obs = (n / S0) * numerator / denominator

print(f"Lee's L = {L_obs:.6f}")

# Permutation test with 5000 random shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 5000
L_perms = np.empty(n_perm)

for i in range(n_perm):
    perm_idx = np.random.permutation(n)
    ghg_perm = ghg_c[perm_idx]
    num_perm = gas_c @ (W @ ghg_perm)
    L_perms[i] = (n / S0) * num_perm / denominator

# Two-tailed p-value
count_extreme = np.sum(np.abs(L_perms) >= np.abs(L_obs))
p_value = (count_extreme + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

print(f"Permutations with |L| >= |L_obs|: {count_extreme}")
print(f"p-value (two-tailed) = {p_value:.6f}")
print(f"Min perm L: {L_perms.min():.6f}")
print(f"Max perm L: {L_perms.max():.6f}")
print(f"Mean perm L: {L_perms.mean():.6f}")
print(f"Std perm L: {L_perms.std():.6f}")
```
